%g-yog 'khor%.english: Here is the third section. Suppose as well that I feel a desire for gain--in the form of money for teaching or the like; or else honor, such as when others prepare a seat upon which I shall teach; or reputation. Or perhaps I may begin to hope for a great circle of servants, or else desire the service of others, who come to honor me by massaging my body. According to your way of thinking, it must be incorrect to do so.

%mi bsrun%.english: Suppose you say the following: "The reason why I don't try to protect all living beings from their suffering is that when this pain comes to them it doesn't hurt to me personally." This though is totally wrong. According to this way of thinking, it must be a mistake for people to try to accumulate money during their younger years out of a concern that they will undergo some kind of suffering during their later years; or for any one of us to try to find some way today, or this morning, to prevent some suffering that we think may come to us tomorrow, or later in the day. Why then do you try to protect yourself from some future pain, from some suffering that you are afraid might come later, since it doesn't do any hurt to you, to the person who exists at the earlier point in time, either? According to your way of thinking, it must be incorrect to do so.

%mi bsrun%.english: Now those who really hope, from the bottom of their heart, to train themselves in the unsurpassed way must first attain their empowerment.  And the very first thing they should do after that is to learn all the fine distinctions involved with the fourteen root vows and other commitments, so that they can keep from ever going over these lines. A person who is not honoring their commitments in this way can talk all they want about practicing the path, or a teaching or learning the secret teachings, but they are surely doing no more than gradually wandering further and further off the path of the diamond way. Those who wish themselves well then must first go and obtain an authentic empowerment, and then as the very foundation of their practice honor their pledges and vows. %mi bsrun%.english: These lines are describing, first, practitioners who have failed to prepare their minds with the path which is shared, and whose hearts are not imbued then by the Wish for enlightenment. Next it describes those who fail to follow the directions they've been given: who fail to honor their pledges and vows.  And then finally it mentions those who have no faith in things like the advices they receive from the Angels and Lamas.  People like this, the verse is saying, will never achieve their spiritual goals; and as such it is crucial for us to put forth great efforts in doing the opposite in each case.

%gnyis gnyis%.english: "In the lines above," one may begin, "you spoke about `the various continents' that came `after that.' Just what are these continents?" Among each of these continents, the first is known as the "Southern Continent of Dzambu." The name derives from the fact that, first of all, it lies south of the ultimate mountain--Mount Supreme. "Dzambu" comes from the sound that comes when the fruit of a dzambu tree drops into the water. And since this mass is surrounded by water, we call it a "continent." [This is a play on words in the Sanskrit, where the word for "island" or "continent" is dvi�pa, meaning "that which divides the water (ap) into two (dvi)."] The continent runs two thousand yojana [about 9,000 miles] on each of three different sides. %gnyis gnyis%.english: One may ask about each of their basic natures. Mental movement is a deed of the thought, for it consists of a deed linked with consciousness of the thought. What it causes--that is, deeds motivated by the mind--are of two kinds: these are deeds of the body and deeds of speech. These two themselves can be further divided into two types each: they are either what we call "communicating" or not.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DE DAG GI NGO BO GANG ZHE NA, SEMS PA NI YID KYI LAS YIN TE, YID KYI RNAM PAR SHES PA DANG MTSUNGS LDAN GYI LAS YIN PA'I PHYIR, SEMS PA DES BSKYED PA'I BSAM PA'I LAS LA LUS KYI LAS DANG , NGAG GI LAS GNYIS, DE DAG LA'ANG RNAM PAR RIG BYED DANG RNAM PAR RIG BYED MA YIN PA GNYIS GNYIS YOD DO,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: sems can rnams la rags pa gnas skabs pa'i lus sems dang phra ba gnyug ma'i lus sems gnyis gnyis yod pa las, ji srid du rags pa'i lus g-yo 'gul sogs kyi bya ba byed pa de srid du gnyug ma'i lus de bzhin lag gi rnam par mi ldang la, rlung rags pa ma lus pa snying ga'i mi shigs pa la thim pa'i stobs kyis lus rags pa g-yo 'gul sogs kyi bya ba byed pa chad pa na gnyug ma'i lus de bzhin lag gi rnam par langs te 'gro 'ong sogs kyi bya ba byed do
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The bodies and minds of living beings come in two different forms: the gross form, the temporal body and mind; and the subtle form, the primordial body and mind.  So long as the gross body is doing what it does--so long as it moves here and there, or anything of the like--then the primordial body cannot rise up in a form which possesses a face and limbs.  There comes a point though where--due to the fact that the gross winds have all dissolved into the indestructible drop at the heart--the normal activities of the gross body, moving here and there and so on, come to a stop.  The primordial body then rises up in a form with a face and limbs, then undertaking itself the activities of coming, going, and all the rest.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: SEMS CAN RNAMS LA RAGS PA GNAS SKABS PA'I LUS SEMS DANG PHRA BA GNYUG MA'I LUS SEMS GNYIS GNYIS YOD PA LAS, JI SRID DU RAGS PA'I LUS G-YO 'GUL SOGS KYI BYA BA BYED PA DE SRID DU GNYUG MA'I LUS DE BZHIN LAG GI RNAM PAR MI LDANG LA, RLUNG RAGS PA MA LUS PA SNYING GA'I MI SHIGS PA LA THIM PA'I STOBS KYIS LUS RAGS PA G-YO 'GUL SOGS KYI BYA BA BYED PA CHAD PA NA GNYUG MA'I LUS DE BZHIN LAG GI RNAM PAR LANGS TE 'GRO 'ONG SOGS KYI BYA BA BYED DO,,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: de'i grangs snyed kyi mi 'gyur ba'i bde ba'i skad cig ma rim par skye zhing , de rnams kyis grangs de snyed kyi las rlung 'gags par byas shing lus kyi bems po'i cha zad par byas te sa gnyis gnyis mngon du byed pa yin te
%gnyis gnyis%.english: While this occurs, a number of moments of bliss equal in number to the drops that have piled up arises within us, one by one.  And these moments of bliss put a stop to an equal number of the winds of deeds, putting an end as well to an equal number of parts of the body's physical material.  In this way we bring forth two levels each.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DE'I GRANGS SNYED KYI MI 'GYUR BA'I BDE BA'I SKAD CIG MA RIM PAR SKYE ZHING , DE RNAMS KYIS GRANGS DE SNYED KYI LAS RLUNG 'GAGS PAR BYAS SHING LUS KYI BEMS PO'I CHA ZAD PAR BYAS TE SA GNYIS GNYIS MNGON DU BYED PA YIN TE,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: sngags la kha sbyor gyi rgyud las, ,rgod dang blta dang lag bcangs dang, ,gnyis gnyis 'khyud dang rnam pa bzhi, ,srin bu'i tshul gyis rgyud bzhir gnas, zhes pa ltar bya rgyud
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The teachings of the secret word can be divided into four, as stated in the Secret Teaching of the Kiss: Flirting, looking, Holding hands, And embracing as a pair: These are the four kinds; They are found In the four groups Living like a worm.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: SNGAGS LA KHA SBYOR GYI RGYUD LAS, ,RGOD DANG BLTA DANG LAG BCANGS DANG, ,GNYIS GNYIS 'KHYUD DANG RNAM PA BZHI, ,SRIN BU'I TSUL GYIS RGYUD BZHIR GNAS, ZHES PA LTAR BYA RGYUD,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: de'i rtsi ma yal ba'i thog ,chos thams cad rang bzhin gyis ma grub pa'i don bsams nas yul stong pa nyid dang yul can bde ba chen po gnyis gnyis su med pa'i ye shes la gdags gzhir byas te
%gnyis gnyis%.english: Try to maintain this feeling, this atmosphere, and then begin contemplating on the fact that no object in the universe has any nature of its own.  This combination--the object of emptiness, and the subject which is great bliss--is the undivided wisdom; and now it is going to get a new identity.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DE'I RTZI MA YAL BA'I THOG ,CHOS THAMS CAD RANG BZHIN GYIS MA GRUB PA'I DON BSAMS NAS YUL STONG PA NYID DANG YUL CAN BDE BA CHEN PO GNYIS GNYIS SU MED PA'I YE SHES LA GDAGS GZHIR BYAS TE,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: On each disk there are two letters, which are meant to stand for Man and Wife.  The letter to your right is the Man, and the one to your left is the Wife.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: YI GE GNYIS GNYIS YOD PA NI YAB YUM STE, GA YAS YAB DANG GA YON YUM YIN,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: de yang thod pa gcig nas mang po bzos pa ma yin par thod pa gcig nas phreng rdog gcig len, de 'dra mang du bsags pa'i pho thod lnga bcu'i phreng rdog lnga bcu dang, mo thod lnga bcu'i phreng rdog lnga bcu byas pa gnyis gnyis spel te brgyus pa yin pas, sngar gyi dam pa 'gas kyang de ltar mdzad pa yod
%gnyis gnyis%.english: You should note here that a "skullbone rosary" is not one where you make a lot of beads from one skull; rather, you go and get one bead from one skull.  You collect beads like this until you have fifty beads from fifty skulls of people who were male, and fifty beads from fifty skulls of people who were female.  When you string the beads then you do so in couples.  A number of holy Lamas from the past have made Their rosaries this way.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DE YANG THOD PA GCIG NAS MANG PO BZOS PA MA YIN PAR THOD PA GCIG NAS PHRENG RDOG GCIG LEN, DE 'DRA MANG DU BSAGS PA'I PHO THOD LNGA BCU'I PHRENG RDOG LNGA BCU DANG, MO THOD LNGA BCU'I PHRENG RDOG LNGA BCU BYAS PA GNYIS GNYIS SPEL TE BRGYUS PA YIN PAS, SNGAR GYI DAM PA 'GAS KYANG DE LTAR MDZAD PA YOD,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: rgyud 'di ru ni dbang bskur ba, ,thams cad kyi ni sgrub por gsungs, ,rgod dang lta dang lag bcangs dang, ,gnyis gnyis 'khyud pa la sogs la, ,dbang bskur bar ni 'gyur ba yin, ,rgyud rnams kun gyi dam pa yin, ,'di ni lha mi zil gnon 'gro, ,zhes pa dang
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The one empowered for this secret teaching Becomes a practitioner of all, it is spoken. They become empowered for all the acts Of flirting and looking and holding hands, Of embracing, one with the other, and such. This one's the ultimate secret teaching, For they then outshine all gods and men.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: ,RGYUD 'DI RU NI DBANG BSKUR BA, ,THAMS CAD KYI NI SGRUB POR GSUNGS, ,RGOD DANG LTA DANG LAG BCANGS DANG, ,GNYIS GNYIS 'KHYUD PA LA SOGS LA, ,DBANG BSKUR BAR NI 'GYUR BA YIN, ,RGYUD RNAMS KUN GYI DAM PA YIN, ,'DI NI LHA MI ZIL GNON 'GRO, ,ZHES PA DANG,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: spyi bor thod pa'i 'og klad rgya'i steng du dbu ma ra ro rkyang gis mdud pa re re bcings pa'i mdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa bzhi thon, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i brgyad, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i bcu drug ,de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i sum cu so gnyis, kha dog khra chol le ba gdugs kha phub pa lta bu dbyibs gru gsum
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The first chakra is located at the tip of your head, underneath the skull and above the brain.  At this point the central channel of taste and the solitary channel both twist around the central channel and form a knot.  From this knot come four major channels.  From the branches of each of those four channels come two more channels making a total of eight.  From each of these split off another two channels making sixteen, and then two more branch off from each of the sixteen making a total of thirty-two.  Its color is that of a multicolored pattern (although oral tradition says to visualize it as white), and its shape is triangular and slightly curved downward like an umbrella facing down.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: SPYI BOR THOD PA'I 'OG KLAD RGYA'I STENG DU DBU MA RA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA RE RE BCINGS PA'I MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA BZHI THON, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I SUM CU SO GNYIS, KHA DOG KHRA CHOL LE BA GDUGS KHA PHUB PA LTA BU DBYIBS GRU GSUM,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: mgrin pa'i aol mdud kyi mtshams su dbu ma la ro rkyang gis mdud re re bcings pa mdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab bzhi, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i brgyad, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i bcu drug ,gdungs kha gyen du bslangs pa lta bu kha dog dmar po dbyibs zlub po
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The second chakra is located at the place of the adam's apple at the throat.  At this place both the channel of taste and the solitary channel wrap around the central channel forming a knot.  From this knot come four major channels.  Then each of these four split into two making eight.  And each of these eight further divides into a total of sixteen.  It is colored red, has a round shape, and curves upward slightly like an umbrella turned upside down.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: MGRIN PA'I AOL MDUD KYI MTSAMS SU DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD RE RE BCINGS PA MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA 'DAB BZHI, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,GDUNGS KHA GYEN DU BSLANGS PA LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR PO DBYIBS ZLUB PO,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: snying gar dbu ma la ro rkyang gis mdud pa gsum re bcings pa'i bjud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab bzhi, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i rgyad, gdugs kha phub pa lta bu kha dog dkar po dbyibs zlum po
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The third chakra is located at the plane of the heart.  Here the channel of taste and the solitary channel wrap around the central channel three times each.  From this knot come out four major channels which each branch into two making a total of eight channels.  It is colored white, has a circular shape, and curves down slightly like an umbrella.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: SNYING GAR DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA GSUM RE BCINGS PA'I BJUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA 'DAB BZHI, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I RGYAD, GDUGS KHA PHUB PA LTA BU KHA DOG DKAR PO DBYIBS ZLUM PO,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: lte ba'i bug pa'i thad du dbu ma la ro rkyang gis mdud pa re re bcings pa'i mdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab bzhi, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i brgyad, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i bcu drug ,de re re las bzhi bzhi gyes pa'i re bzhi'am yang na de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i sum cu so gnyis, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i re bzhi, gdugs kha bslangs pa lta bu kha dog dmar po dbyibs gru gsum rtsa 'dab sbubs stong rtse mo gro sog gris bcad pa lta bu sbom phra 'jag ma tsam 'jam zhing mnyen pa
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The fourth chakra is located at the plane of the navel.  At this place both the channel of taste and the solitary channel wrap around the central channel forming a knot.  From this knot come out four major channels.  Each of these split into two making eight.  Then each of the eight split into sixteen.  Then you can either visualize that each of these sixteen branches off into four making a total of sixty-four channels, or alternatively the sixteen each split into two making thirty-two, and that that these thirty-two each split into two making sixty-four.  The chakra is colored red, has a triangular shape, and curves upward slightly like an umbrella turned upside-down.  The channels are hollow and about the width of a piece of wheat at their outer tips.  They are soft and flexible like the flesh of your tongue.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: LTE BA'I BUG PA'I THAD DU DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA RE RE BCINGS PA'I MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA 'DAB BZHI, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,DE RE RE LAS BZHI BZHI GYES PA'I RE BZHI'AM YANG NA DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I SUM CU SO GNYIS, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I RE BZHI, GDUGS KHA BSLANGS PA LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR PO DBYIBS GRU GSUM RTZA 'DAB SBUBS STONG RTZE MO GRO SOG GRIS BCAD PA LTA BU SBOM PHRA 'JAG MA TZAM 'JAM ZHING MNYEN PA,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Third, how we interpret the object is that every existing thing is nothing more than a label created by our own mind--there is not even an atom's worth of ultimate existence from its own side. The greatest bliss is our subject state of mind, and emptiness is its object.  And this pair of subject and object become like water poured into water--they are unable to be divided, even in a subtle form, into an appearance as two.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: 'DZIN STANGS CHOS THAMS CAD RANG GI BLOS BTAGS PA TZAM LAS RANG NGOS NAS BDEN PAR GRUB PA RDUL TZAM YANG MED PAR NGES PA'I YUL CAN BDE BA CHEN PO DANG YUL STONG PA NYID GNYIS GNYIS SNANG PHRA MOS KYANG BAR MA CHOD PAR CHU LA CHU BZHAG PA BZHIN DU GYUR PA DANG,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: And due to our previous efforts to practice the path, this pure illusory body and the clear light which came before become indivisible one from another.  And these two of our holy body and our holy mind uniting into one is how we achieve the actual union of the two.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DES SNGAR GYI LAM LA BSLABS PAS DAG PA'I SGYU MA'I SKU DE DANG, SNGAR GYI 'OD GSAL DE GNYIS GNYIS MA YIN PA SKU THUGS ZUNG GCIG TU 'JUG PA'I ZUNG 'JUG DNGOS THOB PA NA,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: The first chakra is located at the tip of your head, underneath the skull and above the brain.  At this point the central channel of taste and the solitary channel both twist around the central channel and form a knot.  From this knot come four major channels.  From the branches of each of those four channels come two more channels, making a total of eight.  From each of these split off another two channels, making sixteen, and then two more branch off from each of the sixteen making a total of 32.  The color of this chakra is that of a black and white pattern [although some teachings traditions say to visualize it as white]; its shape is triangular and it is curved slightly downward, like an umbrella facing down.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: SPYI BOR THOD PA'I 'OG KLAD RGYA'I STENG DU DBU MAR RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA RE RE BCINGS PA'I MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA BZHI THON, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I SUM CU SO GNYIS, KHA DOG KHRA CHOL LE BA GDUGS KHA PHUB PA LTA BU DBYIBS GRU GSUM,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: mgrin pa'i aol mdud kyi mtshams su dbu ma la ro rkyang gis mdud re re bcings pa mdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab bzhi, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i brgyad, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i bcu drug ,gdugs kha gyen du bslangs pa lta bu kha dog dmar po dbyibs zlum po
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The second chakra is located at the place of the adam's apple, at the throat.  At this place again both the channel of taste and the solitary channel wrap around the central channel, forming a knot.  From the knot come four major channels.  Then each of these four split into two, making eight.  And each of these eight further divides, for a total of sixteen.  The chakra's color is red, it has a round shape, and it curves upward slightly-- like an umbrella turned upside down.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: MGRIN PA'I AOL MDUD KYI MTSAMS SU DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD RE RE BCINGS PA MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA 'DAB BZHI, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,GDUGS KHA GYEN DU BSLANGS PA LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR PO DBYIBS ZLUM PO,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: snying gar dbu ma la ro rkyang gis mdud pa gsum re bcings pa'i bdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab bzhi, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i rgyad, gdugs kha phub pa lta bu kha dog dkar po dbyibs zlum po
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The third chakra is located at the plane of the heart.  Here the channel of taste and the solitary channel wrap around the central channel three times each.  From this knot come out four major channels, which each branch into two, making a total of eight channels.  The chakra is colored white, has a circular shape, and curves down slightly like an umbrella.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: SNYING GAR DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA GSUM RE BCINGS PA'I BDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA 'DAB BZHI, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I RGYAD, GDUGS KHA PHUB PA LTA BU KHA DOG DKAR PO DBYIBS ZLUM PO,

%gnyis gnyis%.wylie: lte ba'i bug pa'i thad du dbu ma la ro rkyang gis mdud pa re re bcings pa'i mdud mtshams nas phyogs kyi rtsa 'dab bzhi, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i brgyad, de re re las gnyis gnyis gyes pa'i bcu drug
%gnyis gnyis%.english: The fourth chakra is located at the plane of the opening of the navel.  At this place both the channel of taste and the solitary channel wrap around the central channel, forming a knot.  From this knot come out four major channels.  Each of these split into two, making eight.  Then each of the eight split, making sixteen.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: LTE BA'I BUG PA'I THAD DU DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GIS MDUD PA RE RE BCINGS PA'I MDUD MTSAMS NAS PHYOGS KYI RTZA 'DAB BZHI, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BRGYAD, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I BCU DRUG ,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Then you can either visualize that each of these sixteen branches off into four making a total of 64 channels; or alternately the sixteen each split into two, making 32, and then these 32 each split into two, making 64.  The chakra is colored red, has a triangular shape, and curves upward slightly like an umbrella turned upside-down.  The channels are hollow and about the width of a segment of wheat stalk at their outer tips.  They are soft and flexible like the flesh of your tongue.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DE RE RE LAS BZHI BZHI GYES PA'I RE BZHI'AM YANG NA DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I SUM CU SO GNYIS, DE RE RE LAS GNYIS GNYIS GYES PA'I RE BZHI, GDUGS KHA BSLANGS PA LTA BU KHA DOG DMAR PO DBYIBS GRU GSUM RTZA 'DAB SBUBS STONG RTZE MO GRO SOG GRIS BCAD PA LTA BU SBOM PHRA 'JAG MA TZAM 'JAM ZHING MNYEN PA,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: It also says, They possess the nature Of method and wisdom; The upper and lower Joined in union. The letters eh and vam here Are always referred to In couplets. The exact meaning of these last lines is as we have explained earlier, in the reference from the Golden Harvest.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: ,THABS DANG SHES RAB RANG BZHIN GYIS, ,STENG DANG 'OG TU SNYOMS PAR 'JUG ,AE YIG DANG NI Wm YIG NI, ,GNYIS GNYIS SU NI BRJOD PA NYID, CES GSUNGS TE, RKANG PA BZHI PO DE'I DON MAN SNYE LAS SNGAR LTAR BSHAD DO,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Now it's not that you're going to get any definite indications in only one or two sessions; if though you don't encounter any particular obstacles, the flow will start falling into place.  What we mean by "running equal" is that the breath through the two nostrils feels to be running in such a way that the strength of flow is equal: it's not the case that the air is flowing more strongly on one side, and more weakly on the other.  When you get to this point then we can say that you have just started to be able to get the life wind to enter the central channel; you should understand though that it is not the case that you can't experience some lack of movement between the left and the right with even just a single occurrence of the wind's entering.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: DE YANG LAN RE RE GNYIS GNYIS TZAM LA NGES PA MED KYI, 'GAL RKYEN GZHAN MED NA NGES CAN DU THENGS KYIN 'DUG PA DANG, MNYAM RGYU YANG GANG RUNG CIG DRAG LA, CIG SHOS ZHAN PA MED PAR DRAG ZHAN SHED MTSUNGS SU RGYU BA 'ONG BAR SNANG NA, RNAL 'BYOR DE'I STOBS KYIS SROG DBU MAR 'DZUD NUS PA TZAM DU 'JOG NUS MOD KYANG, LAN CIG CHUD NAS GA YAS GA YON RE RE BAR MI 'PHO BA MIN NO,,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: This way of the secret word, the one that utilizes the final result itself, is moreover described in the secret text called The Kiss in the following way: These four modes of behavior-- Flirting, exchanging looks, Holding hands, and embracing One with the other-- Are hidden within the four groups Of the secret teachings, like a worm Eating its way through wood.

%gnyis gnyis%.english: How we bring the winds into the central channel by working at crucial points with a focus during the daytime is clarified by the Lord himself in various books of instruction.  According to these, there are six principal chakras: two at the upper and lower ends of the central channel, and then others where channel petals have split out from the central channel at junctures where it is constricted by knots formed by the the channel of taste and the solitary channel.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: NYIN PAR DMIGS PAS GNAD DU BSNUN NAS RLUNG DBU MAR 'JUG THABS RGYAS PAR RJE NYID KYI KHRID YIG RNAMS NAS GSAL BA LTAR RTZA DBU MA'I YAR SNA MAR SNA GNYIS GNYIS DANG, DBU MA LA RO RKYANG GI MDUD PAS BSDAMS PA'I MTSAMS NAS RTZA 'DAB GYES PA'I RTZA 'KHOR GTZO BO DRUG STE,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: If you wish to do this practice in a very drastic way, then do everything the same as before, only every time it says to hold your breath for a single time, make it a "single time" that lasts for a total of three rounds on the knees and three fingersnaps.   If your physical constitution allows it, hold your breath for one more each of these "single times" during each of the five sessions of the early period of the day.   Add then one each for each of the sessions of the period of the middle of the day, thus doubling to ten by the final session of this period.   By the evening then you have tripled, reaching fifteen by this period's final session.   Continue to increase in this pattern as you meditate over the length of three, five, seven, or fifteen days.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: YANG SHIN TU RTZUB PA'I LUGS BYED NA, GZHAN THAMS CAD SNGA MA DANG 'DRA BA LAS, RLUNG NON PA'I DUS GCIG CES BYA BA'I TSAD NI PUS MO LA BSKOR BA GSUM DANG SE GOL GSUM BSDOMS PA LA GCIG CES BYA STE, KHAMS DANG SBYAR LA SNGA DRO'I THUN LNGA KA LA DE LTA BU LNGA, NYIN PHYED KYI THUN CHUNG LNGA LA RE RE BSNAN PAS GNYIS GNYIS SU BYAS TE THUN CHUNG THA MA LA BCU, DGONGS MO GSUM BYA STE, THUN CHUNG THA MA LA BCO LNGA DE BZHIN DU BSGRES LA, ZHAG GSUM MAM, LNGA'AM, BDUN NAM, BCO LNGAR BSGOM PAR BYA'O,,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: The six groups of the outside rows then transform into six drops, each group becoming a drop.  Each pair of the six becomes an angle of the e syllable.  The e with its three angles then becomes the nature of wisdom; the wam resides within it, indivisible.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: PHYI ROL GYI SDE TSAN DRUG GYUR PA LAS THIG LE DRUG TU 'GYUR TE, SDE TSAN RE RE THIG LE RE RE 'GYUR RO,, DE DAG GI THIG LE GNYIS GNYIS LAS, AE'I LOGS RE RE GRUB PAS, AE GRU GSUM SHES RAB GYI RANG BZHIN GRUB STE, DE'I NANG NA WAm GNYIS MED KYI TSUL DU GNAS SO,, [ALL WAMS HERE S/H CRESCENT]

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Because when these two channels have combined indivisibly the central channel opens, there is also that line which says the "eggshell of ignorance is opened." In this same way all the winds too unite in the central channel at the top, as evam; this same phenomenon is also referred to as the "wind of the mind of wisdom."
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: RTZA GNYIS GNYIS MED 'DUS PAS DBU MA 'BYED PA'I PHYIR, MA RIG SGO NGA'I SBUBS 'BYED PA, ,ZHES GSUNGS SO, ,DE BZHIN DU RLUNG THAMS CAD KYANG DBU MA NA YAR AE WAm ZUNG 'JUG TU 'GYUR TE, DE NYID LA SEMS YE SHES KYI RLUNG ZHES KYANG BYA'O,,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: There are different ways of explaining the first two lines of verse here, but we can start by saying that a certain subject state of mind--the wisdom of great, simultaneous bliss--is perceiving, in a direct way, the object of voidness.  The subject and object then have come to a point where they are indivisible: they are free of any perception of things as being inconsistent, and it is as if water were poured into water.

This is expressed in the lines that go from "Earth and sky are suddenly filled..." up through "...a million kinds of music."  Here we see each offering presented in a group of three or four lines.

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Master Dignaga shows that the Remover beliefs in general are incorrect; and more particularly refutes their ideas on some universal “substance,” and their peculiar version of ultimate freedom.  You can find this in the section of his work which includes the statement, “They use either one relationship each, or else two.”

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Each of the ten bodhisattva levels has its own stages of balanced meditation and subsequent wisdom.  From the second up to the tenth levels, the wisdom at the point just after achieving the level involved has both variations: a path of liberation, and an uninterrupted path.

%gnyis gnyis%.english: The sutra then explains how—even if in the end we are born among human beings—the killing we have done creates a life which has two undesirable results: a shortened lifespan, and many diseases. It goes on to describe two such unwanted consequences for each of the remaining nine negative deeds. Performing the ten positive deeds leads us to a birth among the pleasure beings and humans of the desire realm, all the way up to the level known as “Peak of Existence.”
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: MTHAR GAL TE MI'I NANG DU SKYES NA SROG GCOD KYIS TSE THUNG BA DANG NAD MANG BA GNYIS DANG, LHAG MA DGU'I RE RES KYANG MI 'DOD PA GNYIS GNYIS SGRUB PA DANG, DGE BCUS NI 'DOD PA'I LHA DANG MIR SKYE BA NAS SRID RTZE'I BAR DU SKYE BA DANG,

%gnyis gnyis%.english: Here in this system, the possibility that things could grow from something other than themselves cannot even in a nominal way be correct. We do admittedly accept that, in a nominal sense, a cause is not such that to be it would be to be its result. But this alone is not what is meant by the expression “growing from something other than itself.” It is said that every existing thing has two types of essential natures; which is to say, even though they do possess a kind of essential nature, we do not accept that this constitutes an essential nature where they would grow through some nature of their own.
%gnyis gnyis%.acip: LUGS 'DI LA NI GZHAN SKYE THA SNYAD DU YANG MED DO, ,RGYU 'BRAS GNYIS NGO BO THA DAD PAR THA SNYAD DU 'DOD MOD KYANG DE TZAM GZHAN SKYE'I DON MIN TE, THA SNYAD DU CHOS RE RES KYANG NGO BO GNYIS GNYIS 'DZIN PAR GSUNGS PA LTAR NGO BO GRUB PA YOD KYANG, RANG BZHIN GYIS SKYE BA'I NGO BOR MI 'DOD PA BZHIN NO,,

The two natures of every existing thing

He explains that there are pairs of obstacles that are eliminated specifically at the tenth bodhisattva level, and that these are eliminated in stages. And then with this, we are freed of the terror of the four backwards thoughts. And as we pass beyond that stage, we attain the nirvana where nothing remains.
